name: Ziprasidone
route_note: Oral capsules twice daily with food; IM injection for acute agitation.

discovery.note: Developed in the 1980s–90s as a serotonin–dopamine antagonist with additional 5-HT1A agonism. Year first synthesised at Pfizer, Groton, per Wikipedia.

tagline: Weight-neutral atypical antipsychotic that must be taken with food
summary: Ziprasidone is a second-generation antipsychotic used for schizophrenia and bipolar mania. It causes little weight gain or metabolic change, but prolongs the QT interval more than many alternatives and needs to be taken with a meal for adequate absorption.
mechanism: Ziprasidone antagonises D2 and 5-HT2A receptors, with a high 5-HT2A:D2 affinity ratio, and is a 5-HT1A agonist and 5-HT2C/5-HT1D antagonist. It also moderately inhibits serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake.
Its low affinity for histamine H1 and muscarinic receptors explains its relatively low weight gain and anticholinergic burden.
uses: Acute manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder
Maintenance of bipolar I disorder (adjunct to lithium or valproate)

history.title: Approval delayed
history.detail: An FDA advisory process requires further QT studies before approval.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Geodon is approved for schizophrenia in February 2001.

history.title: IM formulation
history.detail: Ziprasidone becomes the first atypical antipsychotic available as an IM injection for agitation in the US.

history.title: Bipolar mania
history.detail: Ziprasidone is approved for acute mania.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic ziprasidone launches in the US.

history.title: DRESS warning
history.detail: The FDA warns of drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms.

pk.bioavailability: About 60% with food (roughly half without food)
pk.metabolism: Hepatic, mainly aldehyde oxidase; minor CYP3A4

safety.boxed_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; not approved for this use.

facts: Ziprasidone is contraindicated with other QT-prolonging drugs and in recent myocardial infarction or uncompensated heart failure.
